title: Maintaining Proper Pipe Slope for Reliable Drainage
description: Gravity-fed drainage systems rely entirely on correct pipe slope to transport wastewater and solids effectively. If a horizontal drain line is pitched too steeply, liquids rush past solid waste, leaving debris behind to cause blockages. Conversely, insufficient slope fails to achieve the minimum scouring velocity needed to carry waste forward, resulting in heavy sludge accumulation over time. Professional maintenance involves verifying that horizontal runs maintain a consistent, steady grade according to local code requirements and manufacturer instructions. Regular camera inspections help identify sagging sections or improper alignment before complete line failures occur.
